purpose: Cross-check the 11 binomial and two partial labels printed in Estal-Mercado's Daniog River Table 2 against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, preserving the original names and separating nomenclature from identification of the reported specimens.

authority.name: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
authority.institution: California Academy of Sciences, Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability
authority.accessMethod: Official Catalog indexed species and synonym records were checked on 2026-10-31. Some records were available as search-index excerpts rather than directly opened pages. For the exact historical combination Alepes macrurus, the FAO Western Central Pacific guide also explicitly lists it as a synonym of Alepes vari. No access controls were bypassed.
authority.catalogVersion: Online version updated 13 August 2026 where shown on indexed records.
authority.reuse: No item-specific republication license for the Catalog was verified. Only concise attributed nomenclatural outcomes and links are retained.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid name; the Catalog summarizes its known distribution in the western/eastern Atlantic and eastern Pacific records based on Mugil setosus, not the Philippines.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: Major mismatch with the reported Daniog River locality. Treat as a specimen-identification lead requiring voucher or diagnostic-photo review, not proof of absence or proof that the paper's record is false.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid name in the Catalog under Barbodes; Puntius is a historical combination.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: Catalog distribution includes Mindanao, but nomenclature and broad distribution do not verify the Daniog specimens.

Major mismatch: the Catalog summarizes the distribution as Eastern Europe, including the northern Black Sea basin and Crimea. The Daniog identification needs voucher or diagnostic-photo review; the range summary does not itself prove the reported specimen absent or invalid.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid name in Trichopodus; Trichogaster is a former combination. The Catalog summarizes its natural distribution in mainland Southeast Asia and notes introduction elsewhere.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: Possible introduced occurrence or misidentification; the paper supplies no specimen crosswalk to distinguish them.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The printed epithet striate does not match the Catalog's valid spelling striata. Preserve the paper's label verbatim; this is not a specimen re-identification.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: Taxonomic identity unresolved until voucher or diagnostic image is reviewed.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The FAO Western Central Pacific guide explicitly lists Alepes macrurus as a synonym of Alepes vari; the Catalog treats Selar macrurus as a synonym of Alepes vari and lists Alepes vari as valid. Retain the article's source label and do not assume the collected fish was correctly identified.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog records Gerres abbreviatus as a synonym of Gerres erythrourus, despite listing earlier literature that used it as valid. Do not rewrite the study label without specimen-level review.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: Taxonomic name crosswalk does not verify the reported specimen.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid name; the Catalog notes introduction/translocation elsewhere.
nameCrosswalk.localityFlag: A reported Daniog occurrence could be introduced, but source evidence does not establish origin or specimen identity.

interpretation.nomenclature: The 11 binomial source labels were checked for current name status or a likely spelling/synonym crosswalk; the two genus-only labels remain unresolved.
interpretation.specimenIdentity: No voucher specimens, photographs, tissue, or specimen-to-station records were independently reidentified. A catalogue crosswalk cannot establish that the paper's specimens belong to its printed labels.
interpretation.priorityFlags: Request vouchers or diagnostic photographs for Mugil curema and Proterorhinus semilunaris first because their Catalog distribution summaries sharply conflict with the reported Daniog locality. Also review the source spelling Channa striate, genus combination Trichogaster/Trichopodus, and synonym labels Alepes macrurus and Gerres abbreviatus.
interpretation.localPresence: This name-status review adds no independently verified present-day or station-specific occurrence. Historical source labels remain leads only.
interpretation.dietSafetyAndLegal: No diet, bait, water-safety, fishing-rule or catchability evidence was added.
interpretation.publication: Taxonomic status does not settle the article's rights or approve public app use.

limitations: This is a bounded check of the names printed in one historical article, not a full Daniog River inventory or systematic regional checklist.
Catalog distribution summaries are not exhaustive specimen-level range tests and do not establish absence.
No vouchers, photos, DNA, full identification key, or per-site specimen crosswalk were available for this review.
The source article itself has unresolved sampling-date and abundance-total conflicts documented in its separate source review.
Rights for republishing the source-derived checklist remain unverified.
nextAction: Seek the article's voucher/depository details or author clarification for Mugil curema, Proterorhinus semilunaris and the printed Channa striate label; if unavailable, keep all 13 labels research-only and proceed to a separate Daniog-area primary source review.
